name: universal-claim-catalog
note: The 36-claim security catalog (SECURITY.md §4 / MASTER-SPEC.md §9) as adoptable templates. Adopt with: fv-claims add --claim CLM-XXX-NNN. Every template ships UNSUPPORTED: bind scope.controls, models (formalRef), and evidence for your system. Templates state the claim; they contain no evidence about your system.

claims.title: Anonymous reaches only the declared public surface
claims.statement: For every surface s and anonymous actor: grants(s, anon) implies s in publicSurface.

claims.title: Revoked credential grants nothing on any surface after the stated bound
claims.statement: revoked(c) implies no grants(s, c) after propagationBound.
assumptions: revocation propagation bound is documented and measured

claims.title: Expired or rotated-away credential grants nothing
claims.statement: expired(c) or rotatedFrom(c) implies no grants(s, c).

claims.title: No object reference yields another principal's object (BOLA)
claims.statement: Replacing an object id in any id-bearing request never discloses or mutates another principal's object.

claims.title: No function reachable below its privilege floor
claims.statement: For every privileged function f: authority(actor) >= floor(f) before any effect.

claims.title: Mass assignment cannot write protected properties
claims.statement: Client-supplied protected fields (owner, role, tenant, balance) are denied or overridden by server authority on every create/update.

claims.title: Filter/sort/expansion/projection cannot widen visibility
claims.statement: Query results are always a subset of the actor's authorized view, for every query expression.

claims.title: Privileged engines never reachable with record credentials
claims.statement: SQL/raw/replication surfaces require engine-class authority; record credentials grant nothing there.

claims.title: Context resolves before auth; client hints never select it
claims.statement: App/tenant/db context is resolved from server-side authority before authentication; forged hints yield denial, never selection.

claims.title: Credential brute-force is bounded
claims.statement: Authentication attempts are rate-limited with lockout/backoff that encoding/casing variants cannot bypass.

claims.title: No session exists without a valid issuance chain; fixation fails
claims.statement: Every session traces to an issued credential; pre-auth session adoption is rejected.

claims.title: Step-up/MFA state cannot be skipped or replayed
claims.statement: Post-step-up endpoints require a fresh, unconsumed step-up proof bound to the session.

claims.title: Tenant isolation: A's observable behavior independent of B's secrets
claims.statement: Two executions differing only in tenant B's secret data produce indistinguishable observables for tenant A.

claims.title: Realtime subscriptions never emit unauthorized records
claims.statement: Every event delivered to a subscription concerns a record the subscriber may read at delivery time.

claims.title: Search/text/vector indexes never return unauthorized hits
claims.statement: Index query results are a subset of the authorized read view for every query.

claims.title: Errors do not leak cross-tenant existence
claims.statement: Error class (status/body class) for foreign-existent equals nonexistent objects.
assumptions: timing covert channels out of scope (residual)

claims.title: Derivatives inherit source protection
claims.statement: Thumbnails, previews, exports, and cached copies deny exactly where the source denies.

claims.title: Shared-cache keys cannot collide across tenants
claims.statement: Cache keys incorporate tenant context such that no tenant can read another's cached representation.

claims.title: Acknowledged writes survive the declared fault schedule
claims.statement: Every acknowledged write is readable after each executed F-point of the durability class.

claims.title: Uncommitted writes never become visible post-crash
claims.statement: After crash+recovery, reads reflect only committed state; no staged residue is observable.

claims.title: Effects exactly-once under duplication/retry/crash-between-effect-and-ack
claims.statement: No side effect executes twice for one logical operation, under F4/F2 schedules.

claims.title: Migration never leaves a half-live schema; resume is defined
claims.statement: At every crash point, the live schema is a known-good version and migration resumes or rolls back explicitly.

claims.title: Backup publishes only with a valid manifest; corrupt archives refuse by name
claims.statement: publish requires manifest verification; restore refuses corrupt entries naming the entry.

claims.title: Restore starts a new generation; old cursors/tokens/peers fail explicitly
claims.statement: Restore implies generation increase; prior-generation artifacts are rejected with explicit errors.

claims.title: Rollback never discards acknowledged writes
claims.statement: Rollback across the acknowledged boundary fails loudly and leaves acknowledged state intact.

claims.title: Constraints hold in every committed state
claims.statement: No committed state violates declared constraints, including under concurrent writers.

claims.title: Single leader/holder per epoch; fencing rejects stale holders
claims.statement: At most one holder per epoch; writes from stale epochs are rejected by fencing.

claims.title: Quorum-committed entries survive minority loss; no split-brain commit
claims.statement: Conflicting commits in two partitions are impossible; heal surfaces conflicts explicitly.

claims.title: Acks mean durable local apply; unacked work resumes without gaps or dupes
claims.statement: ack implies durable apply; crash before ack replays exactly the unacked suffix.

claims.title: Generation change invalidates all old cursors and frames
claims.statement: After generation change, old cursors/frames are rejected; re-bootstrap is required.

claims.title: Malformed or poison frames rejected without state change or crash-loop
claims.statement: Truncated/replayed/reordered-poison frames change no state and do not wedge the consumer.

claims.title: Replication only from authenticated peers; record clients excluded
claims.statement: Bootstrap/replication requires peer authority; lower credentials are denied.

claims.title: Unfinalized or hash-mismatched uploads are never served
claims.statement: Serve requires finalized status and manifest hash equality.

claims.title: Deletion is durable across caches and derivatives
claims.statement: After delete acknowledgment, no layer serves the object or its derivatives.

claims.title: Jobs: expired leases redrive; poison dead-letters; nothing silently vanishes
claims.statement: Every enqueued message is eventually processed, redriven, or dead-lettered with reason.

claims.title: Resource bounds enforced (payload, pagination, query cost, per-tenant quota)
claims.statement: Declared bounds reject over-limit work before unbounded resource consumption.

claims.title: Secrets never persist, log, or echo outside the secret store
claims.statement: Secret values appear only in the secret store and authorized runtime memory; logs/errors/responses are canary-clean.

claims.title: Only signed, provenance-checked artifacts execute or update
claims.statement: Unsigned, tampered, or provenance-mismatched artifacts are refused at install/update.
assumptions: signing keys managed outside the artifact channel
